done.why: I put the egg in the trophy case early, at turn 26, then kept exploring. Then I went into the dark beyond the Timber Room without a light and a grue ate me. My lantern and matches stayed down there with nobody to carry them. After that the only light I could reach was gone. I was curious and went back down the trap door in the dark and died again. After that there was nothing new I could safely reach, so I stopped.

about: It's a ruined house in a forest, with a whole underground empire under it. There's a flood-control dam, a loud room, mirrors that move you from place to place, and a coal mine full of bats and gas. Your job is to carry its treasures back up to a trophy case. This version has its own small twists. The egg's clasp needs a thief's fingers to open. The mine maze loops back on itself. A narrow passage won't let you through with anything you're carrying, light included.

ending.what: The jewel-encrusted egg sits in the trophy case: "Your collection of treasures consists of: A jewel-encrusted egg." I got it there at turn 26, and it was still there after both of my deaths.

moments.note: I climbed the tree and found the nest with the egg in it right away.
The egg's clasp needs a professional's 'not entirely honest' fingers. It's a clear hint about the thief.
The goal was done in 26 turns. The case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.'
The trap door crashed shut behind me and someone barred it.
The thief wandered through the Loud Room, found nothing worth taking and left, disgruntled.
'take bar' echoed back as 'Bar bar ...'. Saying 'echo' changed the room's acoustics, and then I could take the bar.
I rubbed the mirror, the room shook and I was in a different Mirror Room.
The vampire bat grabbed me and dropped me in the coal mine maze before I could reach the jade figurine.
In the coal mine, rooms lead back into themselves, and every room has the same description. I had to drop items to map it, and batching my moves scrambled my notes.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' I liked the personal touch in the refusal.
The narrow passage refused me even when I carried only the lantern. That forced me to go through in the dark.
A grue ate me in the dark. My lantern was left behind in the Timber Room, and I couldn't get back to it without light.
The second death had new text. My plain belongings were strewn around the forest and the valuable ones had rolled into a dark corner.

wished: Get through the narrow passage past the Timber Room carrying at least a light source
Find any second light source after losing the lantern
Get past the bat to the jade figurine (I picked up the garlic after my first death but never got back underground with it)
Open the egg myself, or get the thief to open it
Explore the attic and the clearing grating (I had no key and no light)
Inflate the plastic boat at the Dam Base

lines.line: The nest is a neat cup of twigs, grass and down, wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
lines.why: It's a charming line, and it told me the egg was what this place is about.

lines.line: The clasp is jeweller's work, and would take a professional's fingers to undo without harm: deft fingers, and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones.
lines.why: It hints at the thief without saying so.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: The trophy case felt like it was waiting for me.
The Loud Room's puzzle came across as a joke.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: The refusal felt written for me rather than generic.

lines.line: The plain things are strewn about the forest and the fields around the house, and anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it.
lines.why: It explained clearly what death had cost me.

fun.why: The early path to the goal was satisfying, and the echo and mirror tricks were fun. The mine maze and losing my light turned the end into a slog.

engagement.why: I kept wanting to open one more area: the dam, the mirrors, the mine. It held me for 244 turns.

difficulty.why: The stated goal was easy (turn 26). The rest is properly tricky, but I lost my light partly through my own carelessness in the dark.

interestingness.why: Familiar bones with real changes: the round room cave-ins, the hint about the clasp, the mine's self-looping rooms, the new text after death.

prose.why: The new lines are witty and well-turned. Some rooms are just a bare name when you come back, which is fine.
